title: Brazilian Portuguese - Fandoms Subject Matter Expert (SME)
description: Project Overview Help shape the future of AI in Brazil! We are building a next‑generation benchmark to evaluate how well AI systems handle complex, real‑world questions in Brazilian Portuguese. This project will help improve how AI delivers accurate, reliable, and context‑aware responses for the Brazilian market. We are seeking Brazilian Portuguese Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) in Fandomsto create high‑quality, expert‑level question‑and‑answer content. This role goes beyond basic data labeling and requires deep domain knowledge, critical thinking, and strong writing skills to test advanced reasoning and contextual understanding in Brazilian Portuguese. Suitable backgrounds may include fandom studies and digital ethnography; senior media analysts with extensive publishing or content strategy experience; anthropology or cultural history of pop culture icons (e.g., Disney, music subcultures), and senior community managers affiliated with major entertainment or fan-led institutions. For digital-discourse profiles, relevant experience may include professional semiotics, internet culture (including political memes); social media sociology; senior-level media education, or recognized digital authorship or public commentary on viral trends. Please submit your resume/CV in English.
min_qualifications: Native or fluent proficiency in Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR) 5–10+ years of professional experience in a relevant field Demonstrated expertise through academic background and/or industry experience Strong analytical skills and the ability to explain complex concepts in a clear, structured manner Excellent written communication skills and attention to detail Ability to work independently and deliver high-quality output in a guideline-driven environment Nice to Have Experience with content creation, research, education, or knowledge evaluation Familiarity with AI training, data annotation, or evaluation projects Background in interdisciplinary work (e.g. media and cultural studies, internet culture, sociology, popular music, film, or digital communities) #LI-CAN17
